resources.string: Read the bands starting from the end opposite the tolerance band, which is usually set apart. The 6th band (temperature coefficient) does not change the value.
Calculates the value and tolerance of a resistor from its colour bands (IEC 60062).
Gives the digit and multiplier band colours for a resistance value, for 4 and 5 bands. The value is rounded to 2 or 3 significant figures.
What is printed on the resistor: 472, 4702, 4R7, 4K7, 01A, A01…
Some 4- or 5-character codes end with a tolerance letter (F = 1 %, J = 5 %…).
Digits with exponent or R/K/M separator

Decodes an SMD resistor marking. In 3 and 4 digit codes the last digit is the number of zeros; R, K and M mark the decimal point (4R7 = 4.7 Ω); in EIA-96 the two digits give an E96 series value and the letter the multiplier.
What is printed on the capacitor: 104, 104J, 4N7, 2A104J, .1…

Decodes a ceramic or film capacitor marking. Three digits: two digits and the number of zeros in pF (104 = 100 nF). R, P, N and U mark the decimal point (4N7 = 4.7 nF). The last letter is the tolerance and, in long codes, a prefix such as 2A gives the voltage.
